text.p: Stock prices fell Wednesday as investors took profits after the blue chip Dow Jones industrial average climbed above the 6,000 mark and planted its flag in record territory earlier in the week.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was down 26.83 points at 5,977.95 after closing above 6,000 on both Monday and Tuesday, despite finishing with a slight decline in Tuesday's session.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 13-9 on active volume of 246 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said Wall Street was also uneasy about the prospect of Democrats riding into Congress on the coattails of President Clinton, which could fan worries about fiscal discipline.
The technology-laced Nasdaq Composite index was down 11.16 points at 1,246.94 after setting two straight record highs on Monday and Tuesday.
Compaq Computer Corp. lost 2-1/8 to 73 after its third-quarter earnings surpassed Wall Street estimates, but analysts said the stock had run up in expectation of a very strong quarter.

"The market was down a bit at yesterday's close, and this is a continuation of that move," said Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities. "The market always takes a little time to adjust to a new plateau and tests it a bit," she said.
But Farley said that despite the profit-taking, some of it by sceptics who do not see the Dow rushing to 7,000 points any time soon, investors were buying on dips.
"You see downturns and recoveries, which indicate that there is buying whenever the market moves down," she said. "There are as many bulls out there, if not more, than there are bears."
Farley said sellers were motivated by profit-taking rather than a rush into cash, something evident in the modest nature of the market's decline.
"There are very few players who anticipate a major correction of any sort," she said.

Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co., said the prospect of Democrats taking over one or both houses of Congress has endangered the division of power between a Democratic president and Republican legislature, which Wall Street liked during the last four years.
"A Democratic victory in Congress would negate the four years of checks and balances and bring into question fiscal responsibility and curtailing entitlements," he said.
Among special situations, Harley-Davidson Inc. jumped 2-1/4 to 46-3/8 after the company reported record third-quarter results.
Sears, Roebuck & Co. was up 3/4 at 49-1/4 after it also reported record earnings.
